summary: Whole-roadmap plan of Euler systems, Kolyvagin systems and higher-rank descent, layers ES.0–ES.8. It imports the 124 targets of the ES.0 part (ES.0–ES.7) and the ES.8 part by node id, and adds 21 targets. The additions complete the sources the maintainer added: Rubin's steps behind the local behaviour of derivative classes (unramifiedness away from pr with a bounded factor, the local lifts at ramified primes, the lifted telescoping identity and the key norm relation, the multiplicative-group example of the congruence, and the derivative classes under the alternative rigidity conditions); the existence of abundant tuples of Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu under its corrected span hypothesis; and Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner's error constants, Chebotarev selection with error terms, module lemmas and rank-one theorem. They also plan the consumer requests addressed to this roadmap: Zhang's residual two-class detection; Nekovář–Castella–Hsieh ring-class anticyclotomic Euler systems with their derivative classes and rational descent; the uniform near-trivial Kolyvagin bound of Castella–Grossi–Skinner and Burungale–Castella–Grossi–Skinner; Zanarella's rigidity, divisibility profile and exact structure theorem for self-dual Kolyvagin systems (with BCGS's 2(M₀ − M_∞) form); Zanarella's equality in Howard's Λ-adic bound for Λ-primitive systems; and the Λ-adic divisibility at the augmentation prime. Every routed item of the four added sources is mapped to the targets that state it (routedItemCoverage). Two clauses of the imported ES.1/selmer-field-saturation are reconciled with confirmed source corrections (assembly.importedNodeCorrections). All nine layers are planned at target level; none is closed.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic twists of a Tate module and their error constants
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve of conductor N, p ∤ 2N a prime of good ordinary reduction, K an imaginary quadratic field with discriminant prime to Np and E(K)[p] = 0, Γ the Galois group of the anticyclotomic ℤ_p-extension K_∞/K with topological generator γ, R the ring of integers of a finite extension Φ/ℚ_p with uniformiser π and r = rank_{ℤ_p} R, and α : Γ → R^× a continuous character. The twist is T_α = T_pE ⊗_{ℤ_p} R(α) with G_K acting through ρ_E ⊗ α, V_α = T_α ⊗ Φ and A_α = V_α/T_α; since α ≡ 1 modulo the maximal ideal, T_α/πT_α ≅ E[p] ⊗ R/(π), so (T_α/πT_α)^{G_K} = 0. The ordinary Selmer structure F_ord on V_α has Σ = {w | pN}, the image of H¹(K_w, Fil⁺_w V_α) at w | p (Fil⁺_w the kernel of reduction on T_pE, tensored with R(α)) and the unramified classes at w | N; it is propagated to T_α and A_α. The error constants are: C_α = v_p(α(γ) − α^{-1}(γ)) if α ≠ α^{-1} and C_α = 0 if α = α^{-1}; C₁ = min{v_p(u − 1) : u ∈ U} for the open subgroup U = ℤ_p^× ∩ ρ_E(G_{K_∞}) of ℤ_p^×; and C₂ the least m ≥ 0 with p^m End_{ℤ_p}(T_pE) ⊆ ρ_E(ℤ_p[G_ℚ]). They satisfy 0 ≤ C₁, C₂ < ∞, U lies in the image of ρ_α for every α, p^{C₂} annihilates End_R(T_α)/ρ_α(R[G_{K_∞}]), C₁ = 0 when ρ_E is surjective and C₂ = 0 when E[p] is irreducible. The combined constants are e_α = r(C₁ + C₂ + C_α) (Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner) and e = r(C₁ + C₂) (Castella–Grossi–Skinner, for α ≡ 1 modulo π^m). The Kolyvagin primes are 𝓛_E = {ℓ ∤ N inert in K : a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p} and 𝓛^{(k)} = {ℓ ∈ 𝓛_E : I_ℓ ⊆ p^kℤ_p}.
hypotheses: E/ℚ, p ∤ 2N good ordinary, K imaginary quadratic with (D_K, Np) = 1 and E(K)[p] = 0
α : Γ → R^× continuous, residually trivial
proofSteps: Finiteness of C₁: ρ_E(G_{K_∞}) = ρ_E(G_ℚ) because K ⊄ ℚ(E[p^∞]) (K is ramified at a prime not dividing Np while ℚ(E[p^∞]) is unramified outside Np; the printed justification is corrected as PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E31 in the register of source mistakes), and ℤ_p^× ∩ ρ_E(G_ℚ) is open in ℤ_p^× (Nekovář, Proposition 6.1.1(i), cited by the source).

Finiteness of C₂: ρ_E is irreducible, so End(T_pE)/ρ_E(ℤ_p[G_ℚ]) is a torsion ℤ_p-module of finite type; since α is trivial on G_{K_∞}, End_R(T_α)/ρ_α(R[G_{K_∞}]) = (End(T_pE)/ρ_E(ℤ_p[G_ℚ])) ⊗ R is killed by p^{C₂}.
Surjective ρ_E gives C₁ = 0 (take u with v_p(u − 1) = 0) and irreducible E[p] gives C₂ = 0 (the image of ℤ_p[G_ℚ] is then all of End by Nakayama).
acceptance: For ρ_E surjective and α of finite order with α² ≠ 1 (a character of the pro-p group Γ has p-power order), e_α = r·v_p(α(γ) − α^{-1}(γ)) and e = 0.
For α = 1 (the untwisted Tate module) C_α = 0 and e_α = r(C₁ + C₂).
The constants depend on E only through ρ_E, so curves whose integral Tate-module representations are conjugate over GL₂(ℤ_p) have equal C₁, C₂.

nodes.title: Chebotarev selection of Kolyvagin primes with error terms
nodes.statement: In the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants put T = T_α, T^{(k)} = T/π^kT, R^{(k)} = R/π^k and ord(x) = min{m : π^m x = 0}. (a) (α ≠ 1.) Let e_α = r(C₁ + C₂ + C_α). For c₁, c₂, c₃ ∈ H¹(K, T^{(k)}) such that Rc₁ + Rc₂ contains a submodule isomorphic to π^{d₁}R^{(k)} ⊕ π^{d₂}R^{(k)}, there are infinitely many ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)}, outside any prescribed finite set, with ord(loc_ℓ c₃) ≥ ord(c₃) − e_α and with R·loc_ℓ c₁ + R·loc_ℓ c₂ ⊆ H¹(K_ℓ, T^{(k)}) containing a submodule isomorphic to π^{d₁+d₂+2e_α}(R^{(k)})^{⊕2}; this second conclusion is vacuous when d₁ + d₂ + 2e_α ≥ k. (b) (α ≠ 1, c₃ = c₁.) There are infinitely many ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)} with ord(loc_ℓ c₁) ≥ ord(c₁) − e_α and R·loc_ℓ c₁ + R·loc_ℓ c₂ ⊇ π^{k−ord(c₁)+e_α}R^{(k)} ⊕ π^{d₁+d₂+2e_α}R^{(k)}. (c) (α ≡ 1 modulo π^m.) Let e = r(C₁ + C₂) and T^{(m)}_E = T_pE ⊗ R/π^m, on which complex conjugation acts. For classes c^± ∈ H¹(K, T^{(m)}_E)^± in the two eigenspaces and every k ≥ m there are infinitely many ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)} with ord(loc_ℓ c^±) ≥ ord(c^±) − e; in particular R·loc_ℓ c⁺ + R·loc_ℓ c⁻ contains a submodule isomorphic to R/π^{max(0, ord c⁺ − e)} ⊕ R/π^{max(0, ord c⁻ − e)}. When ρ_E is surjective, C₁ = C₂ = 0 and (c) has no loss.
hypotheses: the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants; p odd
for (a)–(b): α ≠ 1; for (c): α ≡ 1 modulo π^m and k ≥ m
proofSteps: Restriction to L = K_α(E[p^k]), where K_α trivialises α modulo π^k: by Sah's lemma for an element of G_{K_∞} acting on T^{(k)} as a scalar u with v_p(u − 1) = C₁, the kernel of H¹(K, T^{(k)}) → Hom(G_L, T^{(k)}_E) is killed by p^{C₁}. Only the centrality of that element is used; the printed claim that ρ is injective on Gal(L/K) is not needed (PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E8 in the register of source mistakes).

The restricted homomorphisms f_i lie in the α^{-1}-eigenspace of Hom(G_L, T_E^{(k)}) (PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E27); complex conjugation exchanges the α and α^{-1} eigenspaces, whose intersection is killed by π^{rC_α}, so the projections (1 ± τ)f_i lose at most rC_α in order; for (c) one works directly on the m-torsion, where τ acts, and no C_α appears.

By the definition of C₂ the R-span of the image of each f^±_i contains π^{k−ord(f_i)+r(C₂+C_α)} T_E^{(k)}; on Z = G_L/H (H the common kernel) Nekovář's quadratic-form lemmas produce z ∈ Z⁺ with q(z) ∉ m^{d₁+d₂+2e_α+1} and z outside the preimage Z₃ attached to c₃. The pair (ψ⁺, ψ⁻) needed for the valuation of q exists by a Smith-normal-form choice, although the printed choice is not justified (PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E7).

Chebotarev (Tau Ceti's Chebotarev roadmap, Layer 10) gives infinitely many ℓ ∤ pND_K with Frobenius τz in Gal(M/ℚ), M the field cut out by H; such ℓ are inert in K with a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p^k, so ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)}. Evaluation of the unramified classes at Frob_ℓ² = z² (ES.1/finite-singular-decomposition) gives c_i(Frob_ℓ²) = (g⁺_i(z), g⁻_i(z)), whence the order and span estimates.
acceptance: With ρ_E surjective and α of finite order with α² ≠ 1, (a) with e_α = rC_α recovers the large-image statement of McCallum, Corollary 3.2, up to the C_α loss.
(b) applied with c₂ ∈ Rc₁ is the single-class selection used in the first step of the rank-one argument (ES.4/rank-one-from-nonzero-class).
In (c), letting α → 1 does not increase the loss, unlike (a) where C_α → ∞; this is the input that makes ES.4/uniform-near-trivial-bound independent of m.

nodes.title: Existence of abundant tuples under the corrected span hypothesis
nodes.statement: Setting of ES.1/abundant-tuples: F/F⁺ of degree at most two, R a polarised O_λ-lattice with reductions R̄^{(m)}, fields F^{(m)} ⊆ F₊^{(m)}, γ in the image of ρ̄₊^{(m)} in the nontrivial coset with h_γ the first component of γ^{[F:F⁺]}, and a finitely generated submodule S ⊆ H¹_f(F, R̄^{(m)}) that is free of rank r_S over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}. Assume (i) R_ℚ is absolutely irreducible; (ii) Res_{ρ̄^{(m)}} is injective, for instance by one of the two criteria of ES.1/selmer-field-saturation(b); (iii) the order of γ is prime to ℓ; (iv) (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} is free of rank one over O_λ/λ^m; and (v) the O_λ-span of θ_S(G_{S,γ}) contains λ^c Hom_{O_λ}(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) for an integer c independent of m. Then there are elements Ψ₁, …, Ψ_{r_S} of G_{S,γ}, each the Frobenius of a γ-associated place, which may be taken outside any prescribed finite set of places, such that the image of s ↦ (θ_S(Ψ_i)(s))_i contains λ^{m₀+c}((R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ})^{⊕r_S}. Condition (v) holds with c = 𝔣(r_S)d_R when [F:F⁺] = 1, and the tuple is then (S, γ)-abundant; it holds with c = 𝔣(r_S)d_{Ind R} when [F:F⁺] = 2 and R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠; and it holds when R extends to R₊ over F⁺ and S lies in the 𝔠-eigenspace on which γ acts on (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} by +1. Without (v) the printed Proposition 2.6.6 fails when [F:F⁺] = 2, because G_{S,γ} can be trivial.
hypotheses: (i)–(v) as stated; S free of rank r_S over O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}
d_R the reducibility depth of ES.1/reducibility-depth and 𝔣 the sequence of ES.1/selmer-field-saturation
proofSteps: By (ii) and ES.1/selmer-field-saturation(a), the O_λ-span of θ_S(Gal(F_S/F^{(m)})) contains λ^{𝔣(r_S)d_R}Hom_{O_λ}(S, R̄^{(m)}). Since h_γ has order prime to ℓ, Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) is a direct summand of Hom(S, R̄^{(m)}).

Frobenius elements of γ-associated places land in θ_S^{-1}Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) (the correct inclusion of ES.1/abundant-tuples). When [F:F⁺] = 1 every element of that preimage is such a Frobenius, by Chebotarev in the Galois closure of F_S F₊^{(m)} over F⁺, which gives (v) with c = 𝔣(r_S)d_R; when [F:F⁺] = 2 the realised set is q(N^α), possibly a proper subset, and (v) is the extra hypothesis (PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22/E1 and E23 in the register of source mistakes; the eigenspace and Ind R criteria are recorded there).

For the induced criterion when R_Q is not isomorphic to R_Q^c, use Shapiro to view S inside H¹(F⁺, Ind_F^{F⁺}R). The rational induced representation is absolutely irreducible; apply the saturation bound with its lattice depth. Pairing evaluation on the two coefficient summands commutes with restriction. Average the Galois-closure kernel over the prime-to-ℓ cyclic subgroup generated by a lift of γ: this projection onto fixed points is surjective. Its restriction to F_S is the realised Frobenius set. The fixed coefficient module identifies with R^{h_γ}; projecting the saturation containment proves (v) with the induced depth. For an extending R and an eigenspace S, the same averaging computation has factor 1+εb on the fixed line. It is a unit when ε=b and zero when ε=−b. Compact Shapiro and the coefficient/pairing compatibility are the ArithmeticGaloisDuality supplier inputs, not conclusions of discrete Shapiro alone.

Row selection: over O_λ/λ^n, if the span of a set of vectors contains λ^c(O_λ/λ^n)^r with c < n, then r of the vectors themselves already span a submodule containing λ^c(O_λ/λ^n)^r (Smith normal form over the discrete valuation ring). Applied to the vectors (θ_S(Ψ)(s_j))_j for Ψ ∈ G_{S,γ} and a basis (s_j) of S, with (iv) identifying the λ^{m−m₀}-torsion of (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} with O_λ/λ^{m−m₀}, this yields actual Frobenius elements, not linear combinations of them.
Avoiding a finite set: Chebotarev gives infinitely many γ-associated places with a prescribed Frobenius in Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}).
acceptance: [F:F⁺] = 1, d_R = 0 and r_S = 1: there is a single γ-associated place w with loc_w : S → H¹_ns(F_w, R̄^{(m)}) injective on S/λ^{m−m₀}-torsion.
With (v) dropped, the configuration of PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22/E1 satisfies (i)–(iv) and has G_{S,γ} = {1}, so no abundant tuple exists: (v) is necessary.
The tuple consists of Frobenius elements of places, so ES.4/abundant-localization applies to it with the same loss c.

nodes.title: Residual detection of two classes and classes with prescribed ramification
nodes.statement: Let k₀ be a finite field of characteristic p ≥ 5, V a two-dimensional k₀-vector space with a continuous action ρ : G_ℚ → GL(V) ≅ GL₂(k₀) that is surjective, unramified outside a finite set Σ of primes and equipped with a perfect alternating G_ℚ-equivariant pairing V × V → k₀(1), so det ρ is the mod-p cyclotomic character, K an imaginary quadratic field, τ complex conjugation, and Λ the Kolyvagin primes for V: primes ℓ ∉ Σ, ℓ ∤ pD_K, inert in K, with ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p and tr(Frob_ℓ | V) = 0, so that Frob_ℓ acts on V with characteristic polynomial x² − 1, as τ does. For ℓ ∈ Λ, H¹(K_ℓ, V) = H¹_fin(K_ℓ, V) ⊕ H¹_tr(K_ℓ, V) with both summands two-dimensional and maximal isotropic for the local Tate pairing, each τ-eigenspace H¹_fin(K_ℓ, V)^±, H¹_tr(K_ℓ, V)^± one-dimensional, and the local pairing perfect between H¹_fin(K_ℓ, V)^± and H¹_tr(K_ℓ, V)^±. (a) For k₀-linearly independent c₁, c₂ ∈ H¹(K, V) a positive density of ℓ ∈ Λ, outside any finite set, satisfy loc_ℓ(c₁) ≠ 0 and loc_ℓ(c₂) ≠ 0. (b) Let F be a Selmer structure on V whose local conditions are τ-stable, are their own exact orthogonal complements under a perfect alternating G_ℚ-equivariant pairing V × V → k₀(1), and equal H¹_fin(K_v, V) at every Kolyvagin prime v. For ℓ ∈ Λ, a finite subset S ⊆ Λ not containing ℓ and each sign ±, there is a nonzero c ∈ H¹(K, V)^± with loc_v(c) ∈ H¹_F(K_v, V) for v ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}, loc_v(c) ∈ H¹_tr(K_v, V) for v ∈ S, and no condition at ℓ. Statement (b) does not assert that the singular part of c at ℓ is nonzero.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5, ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k₀) surjective, and a perfect alternating equivariant pairing V × V → k₀(1); this exact GL₂ scope forces k₀ = 𝔽_p because det ρ has image 𝔽_p^×
for (b): self-dual, τ-stable local conditions that are finite at the Kolyvagin primes, as Zhang's Theorem 5.2 provides for Hecke-module quotients of Jacobians
proofSteps: (a) Restriction to L = K(V) is injective on H¹(K, V) because H¹(Gal(L/K), V) = 0 for surjective ρ with p ≥ 5 (the scalar trick of ES.1/selmer-field-saturation(b)). The images of c₁, c₂ cut out an abelian extension M/L with Gal(M/L) ≅ an F_p[Gal(L/ℚ)]-module; by linear independence and irreducibility one finds σ ∈ Gal(M/L) with c_i((τσ)²) ≠ 0 for both i. Chebotarev (Tau Ceti's Chebotarev roadmap, Layer 10) applied to the class of τσ gives ℓ ∈ Λ, and loc_ℓ(c_i) is evaluation at Frob_ℓ² (ES.1/finite-singular-decomposition). This is the special case of McCallum, Proposition 3.1, that Zhang's Lemma 8.1 records.

(b) Compare the Selmer structures relaxed and strict at ℓ (transverse at S): by global duality (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2/selmer-structure-poitou-tate) and self-duality of the local conditions, the relaxed-at-ℓ group exceeds the strict-at-ℓ dual group by the one-dimensional local term H¹(K_ℓ, V)^±/H¹_fin(K_ℓ, V)^± in each eigenspace, so each eigenspace of the relaxed group is nonzero (McCallum, Lemma 5.3, as invoked by Zhang).
The local decomposition and pairing statements are ES.1/transverse-condition and ES.1/transverse-duality specialised to Frob_ℓ = τ on V.
acceptance: (a) with c₂ in the opposite eigenspace to c₁ detects nonzero classes in both eigenspaces simultaneously.
For nonzero linearly dependent classes, for c₂ = λc₁ the statement reduces to single-class detection.
In (b), with S = ∅ the class c is a Selmer class away from ℓ that may be ramified at ℓ; with ℓ replaced by the empty condition it is not claimed.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic Euler systems over ring class fields

planet.name: Anticyclotomic Euler system over ring class fields

nodes.statement: Let f be a newform of weight 2r and level N, p ∤ 2(2r − 1)!Nφ(N), K an imaginary quadratic field in which every prime dividing N splits, with |D_K| > 3 odd (the canonical CM setting of Castella–Hsieh §4.1), T the G_ℚ-stable O-lattice in the self-dual twist V of the p-adic representation of f with its G_ℚ-equivariant perfect pairing T × T → O(1), and χ : Gal(K_{c_o p^∞}/K) → O^× a locally algebraic anticyclotomic character of infinity type (j, −j) and conductor cO_K, c = c_o p^s with (c_o, pN) = 1. Let 𝒦 be the set of squarefree products of primes ℓ inert in K with ℓ ∤ 2pNc_o, K_n the ring class field of conductor n, τ complex conjugation and w_f the Atkin–Lehner sign; choose 𝔑 ⊆ O_K of norm N and let σ_𝔑 be its Artin element. Cohomology is unramified outside the places above pNc_on as in §7.1. An anticyclotomic Euler system for (T, χ) is a family c = (c_n)_{n∈𝒦} with c_n ∈ H¹(K_{cn}, T ⊗ χ^{-1}) such that for every n = mℓ ∈ 𝒦: (E1) cor_{K_{cn}/K_{cm}}(c_n) = a_ℓ(f)·c_m; (E2) loc_ℓ(c_n) = res(loc_ℓ(c_m)^{Frob_ℓ}) along K_{cm,λ} ⊆ K_{cn,λ}; (E3) if χ² = 1, c_n^τ = w_f χ(σ_𝔑)·c_n^{σ_𝔑}. The bottom class is c_K = cor_{K_c/K}(c_1) ∈ H¹(K, T ⊗ χ^{-1}). The families form an O-submodule of ∏_{n∈𝒦} H¹(K_{cn}, T ⊗ χ^{-1}). This is Nekovář's notion, distinct from Rubin's χ-anticyclotomic Euler systems (ES.2/rigidity-variants(c)): the norm relation carries the Hecke eigenvalue a_ℓ(f) of an inert prime, and the tower is the ring class tower rather than ray class fields.
hypotheses: f a newform of weight 2r and level N prime to p; T the Nekovář lattice with its perfect pairing
χ anticyclotomic of conductor c_o p^s with (c_o, pN) = 1

Castella–Hsieh (H)(a)–(c), restricted here to |D_K|>3 odd; no splitting assumption on p. The source also permits 8|D_K in its higher-weight canonical CM setting; this narrower statement does not claim to exclude that case.
proofSteps: The conditions (E1)–(E3) are O-linear equations in the product of the cohomology groups, so the families form a submodule (an equaliser of the corestriction, localisation and conjugation maps).
The bottom class is the corestriction of c_1; under (E1) it agrees with cor_{K_{cn}/K}(c_n)/∏_{ℓ|n} a_ℓ(f) whenever the a_ℓ(f) are invertible, which is not assumed.
acceptance: Generalised Heegner classes z_{f,χ^{-1},nc} satisfy (E1)–(E3) (Castella–Hsieh, Proposition 7.4), and so do their Iwasawa-theoretic specialisations (Proposition 7.8).
For f of weight two and χ trivial, the Kummer images of Heegner points satisfy (E1)–(E3).
The zero family is an Euler system; such a system carries no arithmetic information and every theorem using it needs c_K ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Derivative classes of ring-class anticyclotomic Euler systems and their local conditions at p
nodes.statement: Let c be an anticyclotomic Euler system for (T, χ) in the sense of ES.2/ring-class-anticyclotomic-euler-system, π a uniformiser of O, O_M = O/π^M, T_M = T/π^M T. Fix ν ≥ 0 such that p^ν kills (i) the kernel and cokernel of res : H¹(K, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) → H¹(K_n, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1})^{Δ_n} for all n and M (Δ_n = Gal(K_n/K)) and (ii) H¹(K_v, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) for all v | c_oN, and require the same kernel/cokernel bound for res_{K_c,K_{cn}} for all n and M; put B₁ = min{ord_π(x − 1) : x·I₂ ∈ ρ*_f ⊗ χ^{-1}(G_K), x ∈ ℤ_p^×}. A prime ℓ is M-admissible if ℓ ∤ 2cNp is inert in K, a_ℓ(f) ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod π^M and π^{M+B₁+1} ∤ ℓ + 1 ± a_ℓ(f)ℓ^{1−r}; 𝒦_M is the set of squarefree products of M-admissible primes. For n ∈ 𝒦_M, G_n = Gal(K_{nc}/K_c) = ∏_{ℓ|n} G_ℓ with G_ℓ cyclic of order ℓ + 1 and chosen generators σ_ℓ; D_ℓ = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ} iσ_ℓ^i and D_n = ∏_{ℓ|n} D_ℓ. Writing x = D_n c_n modulo π^M, choose b ∈ H¹(K_c, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) with res(b) = p^ν x and define D_M(n) = p^{2ν}b. This selected descent is independent of b and has res(D_M(n)) = p^{3ν}x; it is not asserted to be the unique preimage of p^{3ν}x, and the derivative class is κ(n) = cor_{K_c/K}(D_M(n)) ∈ H¹(K, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}). Given a Φ-subspace F ⊆ H¹(K ⊗ ℚ_p, V ⊗ χ^{-1}) with orthogonal complement F* (F* = F if χ² = 1), F_M the image of its inverse image in H¹(K ⊗ ℚ_p, T ⊗ χ^{-1}), and the n-imprimitive Selmer group Sel^{(n)}_F(K, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) (finite at v ∤ pn, in F_M at p when p ∤ n), the space ES(T, χ, F) consists of the systems with (E4) c_K ∈ Sel_F(K, T ⊗ χ^{-1}) and c_K^τ ∈ Sel_{F*}(K, T ⊗ χ), and (E5) κ(n) ∈ Sel^{(n)}_F(K, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) for all M and n ∈ 𝒦_M. The classes satisfy (K1) κ(n) ∈ Sel^{(np)}_F(K, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) and κ(1) ≡ p^{3ν}c_K mod π^M; (K2) when χ²=1, for M-admissible ℓ | n, with φ_ℓ : H¹_f(K_λ, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) → H¹_s(K_λ, T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) the finite-to-singular isomorphism (evaluation at Frob_ℓ, then inverse of evaluation at a generator of tame inertia), ((−1)^{r−1}ε_n a_ℓ(f)ℓ^{1−r}/π^M − (ℓ + 1)/π^M)·φ_ℓ(loc_ℓ κ(n/ℓ)) = ((ℓ + 1)/π^M·ε_n − a_ℓ(f)ℓ^{1−r}/π^M)·∂_ℓ(κ(n)), the coefficients read in O; (K3) κ(n)^τ = ε_n κ(n) if χ² = 1, where ε_n = χ(σ_𝔑)w_f(−1)^{ω(n)}.
hypotheses: c an anticyclotomic Euler system for (T, χ) over ring class fields
ν exists (Nekovář's Proposition 6.3, Corollary 6.4 and Lemma 10.1, cited by the source) and B₁ < ∞ (ρ*_f absolutely irreducible with open image)

For the selected descent: p^ν kills the kernel and cokernel of restriction from K_c to K_{cn}. The source states the bound from K to K_n; the relative bound and the identification of the selected lift with the classes in (K1)–(K3) must be proved, not inferred from that wording.

The displayed scalar ε_n finite–singular formula (K2), like (K3), is asserted here only for χ²=1. For nonquadratic χ, complex conjugation transports T⊗χ⁻¹ to T⊗χ; a separate operator-valued/paired relation and its coefficient transport are required (E906).
proofSteps: The identity (σ_ℓ − 1)D_ℓ = ℓ + 1 − N_ℓ and (E1) make x = D_n c_n invariant modulo π^M. The cokernel bound gives a preimage b of p^νx. Two choices differ by a kernel element killed by p^ν, so p^{2ν}b is canonical and restricts to p^{3ν}x. If x already comes from y, this selected lift is p^{3ν}y. The printed uniqueness claim in Castella–Hsieh p. 29 needs this selection or injectivity, not just an annihilated kernel (E904). The relative restriction bound and compatibility with Nekovář’s local formula remain explicit proof obligations.

For the canonical classes in the untwisted setting, Nekovář’s MPIM1990-78 Proposition10.2, printed pp.19–20, proves the unramifiedness and finite–singular formulas using the local comparison of §9. It does not identify the selected bounded lift above with those classes for an arbitrary χ. In the quadratic case (E3) supplies the scalar eigensign. Nonquadratic coefficient transport and the corresponding finite–singular operator remain obligations.

Membership (E5) at p is an extra condition that must be verified for each arithmetic system; for generalised Heegner classes the source verifies it through Bloch–Kato finite parts and corestriction along unramified extensions, and its Lemma 7.5 step needs the correction recorded below.
acceptance: κ(1) ≡ p^{3ν}c_K modulo π^M, so c_K ≠ 0 in H¹(K, V ⊗ χ^{-1}) gives κ(1) ≠ 0 for M large.
For χ² = 1 every κ(n) lies in the ε_n-eigenspace of complex conjugation.

The extra admissibility condition bounds the π-valuation of each coefficient obtained by dividing ℓ + 1 ± a_ℓ(f)ℓ^{1−r} by π^M by B₁. A coefficient is a unit only when its valuation is zero; B₁ = 0 forces this, whereas B₁ > 0 allows a bounded nonunit loss.

nodes.title: Derivative classes are unramified away from pr, finite up to a bounded factor
nodes.statement: Let c be an Euler system for T (ES.2/euler-system-module) over an admissible tower, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, 0 ≠ M ∈ O and r ∈ R_{F,M}, with κ_{F,r,M} the derivative class of ES.3/derivative-class. (a) For every prime Q of F not dividing pr, (κ_{F,r,M})_Q ∈ H¹_ur(F_Q, W_M). (b) If T is unramified at Q, then (κ_{F,r,M})_Q ∈ H¹_f(F_Q, W_M). (c) For every archimedean place w of F, (κ_{F,r,M})_w ∈ H¹_f(F_w, W_M). (d) Let m = sup_{q ∤ p}[W^{I_q} : (W^{I_q})_div], the supremum over primes q of K of the index of the maximal divisible subgroup in the inertia invariants of W = V/T; it is a finite positive integer, independent of M. Then for every r ∈ R_{F,Mm} and every prime Q of F not dividing pr, (κ_{F,r,M})_Q ∈ H¹_f(F_Q, W_M). Part (d) is weaker than ES.3/derivative-local-properties(a) at primes where T is ramified, but suffices for the bounds of Chapter II and for Euler systems of finite depth.
hypotheses: c an Euler system for T over an admissible tower (K_∞ ⊆ 𝒦 with no finite prime splitting completely)
r ∈ R_{F,M} for (a)–(c); r ∈ R_{F,Mm} for (d)
proofSteps: (a): an inertia group I of Q in G_F lies in G_{F(r)} because F(r)/F is unramified at Q; by Lemma IV.4.13(ii) the restriction of κ_{F,r,M} to I is the image of D_{r,F}c_{F(r)}, which vanishes on I since every class γc_{F(r)} is unramified away from p (Rubin, Proposition IV.6.1, from the universal-norm lemma planned in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3).
(b): if T is unramified at Q then H¹_f(F_Q, W_M) = H¹_ur(F_Q, W_M) (Rubin, Lemma I.3.8(ii)).
(c): F(r)/F is unramified at archimedean places, so w splits completely and (κ_{F,r,M})_w is the image of (D_{r,F}c_{F(r)})_{w̃} ∈ H¹(F_w, T) = H¹_f(F_w, T) (Rubin, Remark I.3.7, Lemma I.3.8(i)).

(d): m is finite because the indices are finite and almost all equal to 1; m kills H¹_ur(F_Q, W_{Mm})/H¹_f(F_Q, W_{Mm}) (Rubin, Lemma I.3.5(iii)); apply (a) to κ_{F,r,Mm} and use that m·κ_{F,r,Mm} is the image of κ_{F,r,M} (Lemma IV.4.13(iii)).
acceptance: For T unramified outside p, (b) gives ES.3/derivative-local-properties(a) at every Q ∤ pr with no loss, and m = 1.

For T = T_pE with E of split multiplicative reduction at q, the nondivisible part of W^{I_q} is the p-part of the component group of the Néron model at q, so m can exceed 1 and (d) loses a bounded factor.
The bound m in (d) does not depend on M, so the losses in the Chapter II bounds stay bounded as M grows.

nodes.title: Local lifts of an Euler system at a prime and the finite-part theorem
nodes.statement: Fix an Euler system c for T, 0 ≠ M ∈ O, r ∈ R and a prime q of K not dividing pr, with inertia and decomposition groups I ⊆ D ⊆ G_K. Put W^f_M = T^I/MT^I ⊆ (W_M)^I, 𝕎_M = Maps_cont(G_K, W_M) and 𝕎^f_M = Maps_cont(G_K, W^f_M) with G_K acting by right translation, and Ind_D(W_M) ⊆ 𝕎_M, Ind_D(W^f_M) ⊆ 𝕎^f_M the D-equivariant maps (f(hg) = hf(g) for h ∈ D). For a finite extension L of K unramified at q write H^i(L_q, −) = ⊕_{Q | q} H^i(L_Q, −). (a) For K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞ there is a commutative diagram with exact columns whose columns are the G_{F(r)}-cohomology sequences of 0 → W_M → 𝕎_M → 𝕎_M/W_M → 0, 0 → Ind_D(W_M) → 𝕎_M → 𝕎_M/Ind_D(W_M) → 0 and 0 → Ind_D(W^f_M) → 𝕎^f_M → 𝕎^f_M/Ind_D(W^f_M) → 0, ending in H¹(F(r), W_M), H¹(F(r)_q, W_M) and H¹(F(r)_q, W^f_M), with horizontal maps res_q and the maps induced by W^f_M ⊆ W_M. (b) There are norm-compatible O[G_K]-maps d_{F,q} : X_{F(r)} → (𝕎_M/Ind_D(W_M))^{G_{F(r)}} and d^f_{F,q} : X_{F(r)} → (𝕎^f_M/Ind_D(W^f_M))^{G_{F(r)}} (X_{F(r)} the universal Euler system module of ES.2/universal-euler-system) whose compositions with the connecting maps send x_{F(s)} to (c_{F(s)})_q for every s | r; each is unique up to Hom_{O[G_K]}(X_{F(r)}, 𝕎_M), respectively Hom_{O[G_K]}(X_{F(r)}, 𝕎^f_M). (c) Consequently, for r ∈ R_{F,M} and every prime Q of F above q, (κ_{F,r,M})_Q lies in the image of H¹_ur(F_Q, T) and hence in H¹_f(F_Q, W_M): this is Rubin's Theorem IV.5.1 at primes where T may be ramified.
hypotheses: c an Euler system for T over an admissible tower; the decomposition group of q in K_∞/K is infinite (no finite prime splits completely)
q ∤ pr
proofSteps: (a): 𝕎_M and Ind_D(W_M) are coinduced modules (Tau Ceti's TauCeti.coind with the trivial subgroup and with D), so Shapiro's lemma (TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitShapiro1) and the double-coset decomposition identify the G_{F(r)}-cohomology of Ind_D(W_M) with the semilocal cohomology ⊕_{Q|q} H¹(F(r)_Q, W_M) (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3/semilocal-cohomology); 𝕎_M has trivial higher cohomology. The left column is ES.3/lifting-to-induced-module(a).

(b): the classes (c_{F(s)})_Q are unramified (Rubin, Proposition IV.6.1), so the map X_{F(r)} → H¹(F(r)_q, W_M) factors through H¹(F(r)_q, W^f_M). Choose a ℤ_p-extension K′_∞ ⊆ K_∞ in which q has finitely many primes; then the inverse limit of H⁰(F(r)_q, W_M) over the tower vanishes (Rubin, Lemma B.3.2) and each H¹(F(r)_q, W_M) is finite, so the limit of the right column is short exact; the limit of (𝕎^f_M)^{G_{F(r)}} is free over (O/M)[[Gal(K_∞(r)/K)]], and the Ext¹-vanishing of ES.2/universal-euler-system lifts X_{∞,r} to the middle term; descend to finite level by the freeness of X_{∞,r}.

(c): compare the image of the global lift d of ES.3/lifting-to-induced-module(b) with d^f_{F,q} in the middle column; by uniqueness they differ by an element of Hom(X_{F(r)}, (𝕎_M)^{G_{F(r)}}), which on D_{r,F}x_{F(r)} lands in the kernel of the connecting map by ES.3/derivative-invariance. Hence (κ_{F,r,M})_Q comes from H¹(F_Q, T^{I_Q}/MT^{I_Q}); combined with ES.3/derivative-classes-unramified(a) it comes from H¹(F_Q^ur/F_Q, T^{I_Q}/M), and since Gal(F_Q^ur/F_Q) ≅ Ẑ has cohomological dimension one, H¹_ur(F_Q, T) surjects onto that group; Rubin's Lemmas I.3.5(ii) and I.3.8(i) place the image in H¹_f.

For X=T^{I_Q}, a finite free ℤ_p-module, identify continuous cochains with the inverse limit for X/p^aX. H¹(Ẑ,X/p^aX) is finite, hence its tower is Mittag-Leffler. The Milnor sequence gives H²(Ẑ,X)=0 because H² of every finite discrete quotient vanishes. The quotient X→X/MX has a continuous section, so the compact long exact sequence gives surjectivity on H¹. Do not extend this argument to an arbitrary profinite coefficient module without the limit hypotheses.
acceptance: If T is unramified at q then W^f_M = W_M, Ind_D(W^f_M) = Ind_D(W_M), the right and middle columns coincide and (c) reduces to ES.3/derivative-classes-unramified(b).
For r = 1, (c) says (c_F)_Q mod M lies in H¹_f(F_Q, W_M), as it must since c_F is a universal norm.
The hypothesis that the decomposition group of q in K_∞/K is infinite is used to kill the inverse limit of local H⁰; for a finite decomposition group the lift need not exist.

nodes.title: The lifted telescoping identity and the key norm relation for lifts
nodes.statement: Fix an Euler system c for T, 0 ≠ M ∈ O, r ∈ R, a prime q ∈ R_{K,M} not dividing r, K ⊂_f F ⊂ K_∞, a prime Q of K̄ above q with inertia and decomposition groups I ⊆ D, a lift σ_q ∈ I of the generator of Γ_q and a Frobenius Fr_q ∈ D. Put m = [K(q) : K(1)], N_q = Σ_{i=1}^{m} σ_q^i and D_q = Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} iσ_q^i in ℤ[I]. (a) (σ_q − 1)D_q = mσ_q^m − N_q in ℤ[I] (the lifted telescoping identity; σ_q^m ≠ 1 in I). (b) If d : X_{F(r)} → 𝕎_M/W_M lifts c as in ES.3/lifting-to-induced-module and d̂(x_{F(r)}) ∈ 𝕎_M lifts d(x_{F(r)}), then σσ′γd̂(x_{F(r)}) = σ′σγd̂(x_{F(r)}) for all γ ∈ G_K and σ, σ′ ∈ D; this can fail for σ, σ′ outside D. (c) For a lift d : X_{F(rq)} → 𝕎_M/W_M of c and lifts d̂(x_{F(rq)}), d̂(x_{F(r)}) ∈ 𝕎_M, N_q γ d̂(x_{F(rq)}) − P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; Fr_q^{-1}) γ d̂(x_{F(r)}) ∈ W_M is independent of the choices and is zero in W_M for every γ ∈ G_K. (d) Consequently, with Q_q(x) ∈ (O/M)[x] the unique polynomial with (x − 1)Q_q(x) ≡ P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; x) mod M, κ_{F,rq,M}(σ_q) = Q_q(Fr_q^{-1})κ_{F,r,M}(Fr_q) in W_M for cocycles representing the derivative classes: the singular part of κ_{F,rq,M} at q is φ^fs_q of the finite part of κ_{F,r,M} (ES.3/derivative-local-properties(b)).
hypotheses: c an Euler system for T over an admissible tower; q ∈ R_{K,M}, so M | [K(q) : K(1)] and M | P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; 1)
T unramified at q
proofSteps: (a) is the telescoping computation of ES.3/derivative-operators carried out in ℤ[I] without imposing σ_q^m = 1.

(b): T is unramified at q, so every cocycle representing γc_{F(r)} vanishes on I ∩ G_{F(r)} (Rubin, Proposition IV.6.1), hence (σ − 1)γd̂(x_{F(r)}) = 0 for σ ∈ I ∩ G_{F(r)} by the cocycle formula of ES.3/lifting-to-induced-module; the commutator subgroup of D lies in I ∩ G_{F(r)} because D/I and Gal(F(r)/K) are abelian.

(c): independence of the choices uses that σ_q fixes W_M, that M | [K(q) : K(1)] and that P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; Fr_q^{-1}) kills W_M (ES.2/euler-polynomial). For vanishing, pass to F′ ⊆ K_∞ in which the decomposition group of q in F′(rq)/F(rq) has order divisible by k_pM (possible because the decomposition group in K_∞ is infinite), write the norm as N′N″ with N′ the sum over the powers of Fr_q^k, and use (b) to commute N′ past N_q and P(Fr_q^{-1}); the difference lies in N′W_M ⊆ |H|W_M = 0.

(d): by the cocycle formula κ_{F,r,M}(Fr_q) = (Fr_q − 1)D_{r,F}d̂(x_{F(r)}) and κ_{F,rq,M}(σ_q) = (σ_q − 1)D_{rq,F}d̂(x_{F(rq)}); expand with (a), use (b) to commute elements of O[D], and (c) with M | m to conclude.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, T = ℤ_p(1) and q = ℓ a prime with M | ℓ − 1, P(Fr_ℓ^{-1} | T*; x) = 1 − x and Q_ℓ = −1, so (d) says the singular part of κ_{rℓ} at ℓ is minus the image of the finite part of κ_r: Kolyvagin's relation for cyclotomic units up to sign conventions.
Example of (b) failing outside D: for σ, σ′ ∈ G_K with non-commuting images in Gal(K(W_M)K(r)/K), σσ′d̂ and σ′σd̂ can differ because the action on d̂ does not factor through an abelian extension.
With M replaced by M′ dividing M, the identities in (c)–(d) reduce compatibly.

nodes.title: Worked example: Kolyvagin's congruence for the multiplicative group
nodes.statement: Let T = ℤ_p(1), so H¹(F(r), T) is the p-adic completion of F(r)^× and, for a prime Q of F(r) not dividing p with residue field k_Q, H¹_f(F(r)_Q, T) = H¹_ur(F(r)_Q, T) ≅ k_Q^× ⊗ ℤ_p; full local H¹ is the completion of F(r)_Q^× and also has the valuation summand ℤ_p. Then P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; x) = 1 − x and the congruence of ES.3/congruence reads: for every r ∈ R, prime q with rq ∈ R and prime Q of F(r) above q, the element c_{F(rq)} / c_{F(r)}^{((N(q) − 1)/[K(q):K(1)]) Fr_q^{-1}} has order prime to p in k_Q^×, that is, the two classes agree in the p-adic completion of k_Q^×. For the cyclotomic-unit Euler system this is the p-part of the congruence 1 − ζ_{rq} ≡ 1 − ζ_r^{Fr_q^{-1}} modulo every prime above q, which holds because ζ_q ≡ 1 there. Kolyvagin's original definition imposed this congruence as an axiom; under Rubin's definition, which requires the system to extend along a ℤ_p^d-extension, it is a theorem (ES.3/congruence), and conversely the congruence allows one to drop the ℤ_p^d-extension (rigidity condition (ii)′(c) of ES.2/rigidity-variants).
hypotheses: T = ℤ_p(1); c an Euler system for T over an admissible tower
proofSteps: For T = ℤ_p(1), T* = Hom(T, ℤ_p(1)) = ℤ_p with trivial action, so det(1 − Fr_q^{-1}x | T*) = 1 − x.

(P_q(Fr_q^{-1}) − P_q(N(q)Fr_q^{-1}))/[K(q) : K(1)] = ((N(q) − 1)/[K(q) : K(1)])Fr_q^{-1}. The 1999 draft prints the denominator [K(q) : K] in Example IV.8.2; the published Example 4.8.2 has [K(q) : K(1)], as Corollary IV.8.1 requires (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems/E901 in sourceIssues). The two agree when K(1) = K, for instance for K = ℚ.

Local Kummer theory gives H¹(L, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim_a L^×/(L^×)^{p^a}. For residue characteristic different from p, reduction identifies the completed units with k_L^× ⊗ ℤ_p, and valuation gives a split exact sequence 0 → k_L^× ⊗ ℤ_p → H¹(L, ℤ_p(1)) → ℤ_p → 0. Euler-system classes at q lie in the finite/unramified subgroup by ES.2/classes-unramified-outside-p. Their unit reductions give the stated congruence. The full-group identification printed in both Rubin examples omits the valuation term (E902).
acceptance: For K = ℚ, r = 1 and the cyclotomic units c_{ℚ(q)} = N(1 − ζ_q) (suitably smoothed), the congruence says the unit is a p-th power residue up to the stated exponent modulo primes above q.
For q ∈ R with N(q) ≡ 1 modulo a high power of p the exponent (N(q) − 1)/[K(q) : K(1)] is a p-adic unit times a power of p, so the statement is nontrivial exactly on the p-part of k_Q^×.

nodes.title: Module lemmas for the self-dual induction over a discrete valuation ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and finite residue field. For a finitely generated torsion R-module X write X ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{s(X)} R/π^{d_i(X)} with d₁(X) ≥ ⋯ ≥ d_{s(X)}(X) > 0 and exp(X) = d₁(X) (exp(0) = 0). (a) If N ⊆ M then s(N) ≤ s(M) and d_i(N) ≤ d_i(M) for 1 ≤ i ≤ s(N). (b) Consider exact sequences 0 → X → R/π^k ⊕ M → R/π^{k−a} ⊕ R/π^b → 0 and 0 → X → R/π^k ⊕ M′ → R/π^{a′} ⊕ R/π^{k−b′} → 0 of finite R-modules, where M and M′ are each a direct sum of two isomorphic modules, 2s = dim M[π], 2s′ = dim M′[π], k > exp(M) + 2a and a′ ≤ a. Fix M = ⊕_{i=1}^{2s} M_i with M_i ≅ R/π^{d_i(M)} and d₁(M) = d₂(M) ≥ d₃(M) = d₄(M) ≥ ⋯. Then (i) s − 1 ≤ s′ ≤ s + 1; (ii) b ≤ exp(M); (iii) exp(X) ≤ exp(M) + a; (iv) if s > 0 there is an index 1 ≤ i₀ ≤ 2s with ⊕_{i ≠ i₀} M_i ↪ X, while if s = 0 only the trivial injection 0 ↪ X is asserted; (v) there is an injection X ↪ M′ ⊕ R/π^{exp(X)}; (vi) d_i(M′) ≥ d_{i+2}(M) for 1 ≤ i ≤ 2s − 2 (an empty range when s ≤ 1).
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring; all modules finitely generated and torsion
for (b): the two exact sequences, M and M′ doubled modules, k > exp(M) + 2a and a′ ≤ a
proofSteps: (a): s(N) = dim N[π] ≤ dim M[π]; induct on s(N) by passing to N/N[π^d] ⊆ M/M[π^d] with d = d_{s(N)}(N), and count dim N[π^d]/N[π^{d−1}] ≤ dim M[π^d]/M[π^{d−1}].

(i): the minimal number of generators changes by at most one across each sequence, by (a); (ii): since k − a > exp(M), the free summand R/π^k maps onto a summand of order max(k − a, b), so M surjects onto R/π^{min(k−a, b)}; (iii): X/(X ∩ R/π^k) embeds in M and X ∩ R/π^k ≅ R/π^a.

(iv): when s > 0, the image of the map in the first sequence is R/π^{k−a} plus the image of one summand M_{i₀}, so X surjects onto ⊕_{i≠i₀} M_i, and Pontryagin self-duality of finite R-modules turns this into an injection; when s = 0 no index is chosen (the printed statement omits this case: PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E43 in the register of source mistakes).

(v): the free summand maps onto R/π^{k−b′}: the order o of the image of 1 satisfies o > a′ because k − o ≤ exp(X) < k − a′, and o ≤ max(a′, k − b′) (the printed argument names the wrong module, PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E28); then X is an extension of a cyclic module by M″ ⊆ M′ and duality gives the injection. (vi) combines (iv), (v) and (a).
acceptance: N = R/π ⊆ M = R/π² ⊕ R/π (N the socle of the first summand): s(N) = 1 ≤ 2 and d₁(N) = 1 ≤ 2.
With M = 0 (s = 0) the first sequence forces b = 0 and X ≅ R/π^a, and (iv) asserts nothing beyond 0 ↪ X; there is no summand to omit.
The doubling hypothesis makes dim M[π] even, so s is an integer; the self-dual Cassels structure of ES.4/weak-cassels-structure supplies it.

nodes.title: Rank one from a nonzero Kolyvagin class, with an explicit exponent bound
nodes.statement: In the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants with α ≠ 1, let (T, F, 𝓛) = (T_α, F_ord, 𝓛_E), e_α = r(C₁ + C₂ + C_α), and let ε ∈ {0, 1} and M^{(k)}(n) be as in ES.4/weak-cassels-structure. If κ ∈ KS(T, F, 𝓛) has κ₁ ≠ 0 in H¹(K, T), then ε = 1, H¹_F(K, T) ≅ R, and for k ≫ 0 every element of M^{(k)}(1) has order < k. Quantitatively, let s = ind(κ₁) be the largest j with κ₁ ∈ m^j H¹_F(K, T); for every k > s + 3e_α, writing the image of κ₁ in H¹_F(K, T^{(k)}) as π^s c₁, the quotient H¹_F(K, T^{(k)})/Rc₁ is killed by π^{s+3e_α}, so exp M^{(k)}(1) ≤ ind(κ₁) + 3e_α.
hypotheses: the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants, α ≠ 1, p odd
κ a Kolyvagin system for (T_α, F_ord, 𝓛_E) with κ₁ ≠ 0
proofSteps: For k large the image of κ₁ in H¹_F(K, T^{(k)}) is nonzero with the same index s; write it as π^s c₁ with Rc₁ ≅ R^{(k)}. Let c₂ ∉ Rc₁ and d the order of its image modulo Rc₁, so Rc₁ + Rc₂ ⊇ R^{(k)} ⊕ π^{k−d}R^{(k)}.
ES.1/error-tolerant-chebotarev(b) gives ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)} with ord(loc_ℓ c₁) ≥ k − e_α and R·loc_ℓ c₁ + R·loc_ℓ c₂ ⊇ π^{e_α}R^{(k)} ⊕ π^{k−d+2e_α}R^{(k)}.

The finite–singular relation gives ord(loc^s_ℓ κ_ℓ) = ord(loc_ℓ κ₁) ≥ k − s − e_α, with κ_ℓ ∈ H¹_{F(ℓ)}(K, T^{(k)}) (the source writes H¹_F: PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E25). Global duality between T_α and T_{α^{-1}} (complex conjugation maps κ_ℓ to the α^{-1}-side relaxed group), with loc_ℓ of H¹_F and loc^s_ℓ of the relaxed group exact annihilators (ES.1/transverse-duality), yields k − s − e_α ≤ k − d + 2e_α, so d ≤ s + 3e_α.

Hence H¹_F(K, T^{(k)})/Rc₁ is killed by π^{k−1} when k > s + 3e_α, which forces ε ≤ 1; ε = 0 is excluded directly (c₁ of order k in M^{(k)}(1)^{⊕2} would give an element of order k in the quotient), replacing the source's unjustified torsion-freeness step (PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E11). The index is the largest j with κ₁ ∈ m^j H¹ (the printed parenthetical is a misprint, PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22/E26).
acceptance: With ρ_E surjective (C₁ = C₂ = 0, so e_α = rC_α), the bound reads exp M^{(k)}(1) ≤ ind(κ₁) + 3rC_α.
If κ₁ = 0 the theorem says nothing; the stub theory of ES.4/stub-sheaf is needed for systems with vanishing bottom class.
The quantitative exponent bound is the base case n₀ = 1 of the induction in ES.4/howard-descent-with-errors.

planet.name: Uniform Kolyvagin bound near the trivial character

nodes.statement: In the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants: (a) there are integers M₀, E ≥ 0 depending only on T_pE and rank_{ℤ_p} R such that, for every nontrivial anticyclotomic α ≡ 1 mod π^m with m ≥ M₀ and every κ ∈ KS(T_α, F_ord, 𝓛_E) with κ₁ ≠ 0, H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α) has R-rank one and H¹_{F_ord}(K, A_α) ≅ Φ/R ⊕ M ⊕ M with length_R(M) ≤ length_R(H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α)/Rκ₁) + E. The error E does not depend on m, in contrast with E_α of ES.4/howard-descent-with-errors, which grows as α → 1. (b) (Rescaled systems; R = ℤ_p.) Let 𝓛 ⊆ 𝓛_E contain 𝓛_e = {ℓ : a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p^e} for e ≫ 0. Suppose {κ̃_n ∈ H¹(K, T_α/I_nT_α)}_{n∈N(𝓛)} is a family with κ̃₁ ≠ 0 and that for some t ≥ 0, independent of n, {p^t κ̃_n} is a Kolyvagin system for (T_α, F_ord, 𝓛); the family {κ̃_n} itself need not be one. Then there are M₀, E depending only on T_pE such that for m ≥ M₀, H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α) has ℤ_p-rank one and H¹_{F_ord}(K, A_{α^{-1}}) ≅ ℚ_p/ℤ_p ⊕ M ⊕ M with length(M) ≤ length(H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α)/ℤ_p κ̃₁) + E; the error is independent of t, and E = 0 when ρ_E is surjective. (c) The same statement as (a) holds for the self-dual twist of the Galois lattice of a weight-2r newform at an Eisenstein prime, with C₁ defined through scalar matrices in its image.
hypotheses: the setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants; α nontrivial with α ≡ 1 mod π^m
for (b): R = ℤ_p, 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_e for e ≫ 0, and a fixed t ≥ 0 with {p^t κ̃_n} a Kolyvagin system

For the higher-weight branch: f is a normalized weight-2r newform of trivial nebentype, p∤2N is ordinary and Eisenstein, O is the coefficient completion, T is its chosen self-dual-twist lattice with H⁰(K,T/πT)=0, every prime dividing N splits in K, p splits in K, and D_K is odd, prime to Np and not −3 (Keller–Yin introduction and §3).
proofSteps: Rank one: ES.4/rank-one-from-nonzero-class; its proof gives M^{(k)}(1) ≅ M₀ for k > ind(κ₁) + 3r(C₁ + C₂ + m), so the CGLS error, which contains C_α ≈ m, cannot be used directly for the bound.

Work on the π^m-torsion with complex conjugation and the Chebotarev loss e=r(C₁+C₂), independent of α. CGS §6.4 pp.24–28 constructs at most ρ steps, ρ=2(ρ_e(1)−1), where ρ_t counts cyclic summands of length greater than t in both signs. Conditions(a)–(e) bound the residual number of summands, module-length changes, and class indices; (f) increases the threshold by between two and five multiples of e, while (g) makes the surviving large-summand count drop every two steps. Summing the length/index inequalities yields a bound with E=(ρ+(s(1)+1+2ρ)(5ρ+1))e and closeness threshold M₀=(1+5ρ)e, with s(1)=dim_F H¹_F(K,T^(1))−1. The auxiliary torsion precision k is chosen above the initial length, index and m terms; only M₀ and E must be independent of m. This is a target-level proof, not a promise to add one node per inductive inequality.

(b): choose f ≫ 0 with κ̃₁ ≢ 0 mod p^f and 𝓛_{f+t} ⊆ 𝓛; the classes κ̃_n give a nontrivial Kolyvagin system modulo p^f for 𝓛_{f+t}, and the inductive argument needs only ord(loc_ℓ κ̃_ℓ) = ord(loc_ℓ κ̃₁) ≥ ord(κ̃₁) − e at the first prime, which follows from the relation for p^tκ̃ once k > t + f.

For (c), use the stated higher-weight setting and the existence of a nontrivial scalar in the Galois image (Keller–Yin Lemma3.0.3). Transport the ordinary filtration of the untwisted modular lattice before the self-dual Tate twist; its rank-one quotient is no longer unramified after a nonzero twist. The α-independent Chebotarev argument and the module induction then apply with constants depending on T and the coefficient rank.
acceptance: For ρ_E surjective, (b) with t = 0 recovers Howard's bound for the Heegner Kolyvagin system with no error term.
Applied at α = α_m ≡ 1 mod π^m with m → ∞ and combined with control theorems, (a) yields the divisibility at the augmentation prime of ES.8/augmentation-prime-divisibility.
(a) is stated only for α close to 1; for α far from 1 the bound of ES.4/howard-descent-with-errors applies with error E_α.

nodes.title: Rational Kolyvagin descent for ring-class anticyclotomic Euler systems
nodes.statement: In the setting of ES.3/ring-class-derivative-classes, assume Hypothesis (H)(a)–(c) of Castella–Hsieh §6: p ∤ 2(2r − 1)!Nφ(N); every prime dividing N splits in K, and, if r > 1, either |D_K| > 3 is odd or 8 | D_K (existence of a canonical CM elliptic curve); and (c_o, N) = 1. (a) If c ∈ ES(T, χ, F) has c_K ≠ 0 in H¹(K, V ⊗ χ^{-1}), then Sel_{F*}(K, V ⊗ χ) = Φ·c_K^τ, Φ = O[1/p]: the Selmer group of V ⊗ χ with local condition F* at p is the line spanned by the conjugate of the bottom class. (b) (Complementary local class.) Suppose further that p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, f is ordinary at p and χ has infinity type (j, −j) with j ≥ r, and let z^χ be the χ-specialisation of the Iwasawa class of generalised Heegner cycles. If loc_p(z^{χ^{-1}}) ≠ 0, then the Bloch–Kato Selmer group Sel(K, V ⊗ χ) vanishes. The statement is rational: it bounds the Φ-dimension, not the length of an integral Selmer module.
hypotheses: Castella–Hsieh Hypothesis (H)(a)–(c): p ∤ 2(2r − 1)!Nφ(N); every prime dividing N splits in K, with |D_K| > 3 odd or 8 | D_K when r > 1; (c_o, N) = 1
c ∈ ES(T, χ, F) with c_K non-torsion; for (b) additionally p split in K, f ordinary, j ≥ r

This is a conditional descent target: the canonical selected derivative’s relative restriction control and (K1)–(K3) compatibility, including the nonquadratic paired local relation, must first be proved. The class construction is not claimed complete by this node.
proofSteps: Image lemmas: with H♭ the maximal pro-p subextension of K_{c_o} in the ring class field cutting out χ mod π^M, ℚ^{ker ρ*_f} ∩ H♭ = ℚ (a p-ramified abelian subextension of K_{c_o p^∞} is ℚ or ℚ(√p*)), so ρ*_f(G_ℚ) = ρ*_f(G_{H♭}); B₂ = min{n : π^n M₂(O) ⊆ O[ρ*_f(G_ℚ)]} bounds the failure of R_ρ-submodules to be large, and Nekovář's lemmas give π^{(2^{s+1}−2)B₂}V_S ⊆ O[G_S] for the Galois group cut out by an s-generated submodule S.
Prime selection: π^{B₁} kills H¹(Gal(L/K), T_M ⊗ χ^{-1}) (a scalar in the image), and Chebotarev gives infinitely many inert ℓ with prescribed Frobenius g ∈ G_S^+ that are M-admissible.

Descent: with B₃ the divisibility of c_K, B₄ = 0 if χ² = 1 and min ord_π(χ²(σ) − 1) otherwise, C₁ = 6B₂ + B₁ + B₃ + B₄ and M > 2C₁ + 2B₁, choose ℓ₁ with ord_π α_{ℓ₁}(κ(1)) ≤ C₁ and then a second prime making the pair (κ(1), κ(ℓ₁)) large; the relations (K1)–(K3) and global duality bound Sel_{F*}(K, T_M ⊗ χ)/(O·κ(1)^τ) by a constant independent of M, which gives (a) after inverting p.

(b): apply (a) to the specialisations of the Iwasawa classes, with F the orthogonal complement of the line spanned by loc_v(z^χ) at v | p, and use the Poitou–Tate sequence; for j ≥ r the Bloch–Kato condition is relaxed at one prime above p and strict at the other. The verification that these classes satisfy (E5) uses a corestriction step that the authors correct in the footnote to Proposition 7.8.
acceptance: For χ = 1, r = 1 and Heegner points, (a) is the rational form of Kolyvagin's theorem: a non-torsion Heegner point spans the Selmer group of V = V_pE over Φ.
If c_K is torsion the theorem gives nothing; the integral exponent bound needs the error-tolerant theory of this layer.
(b) concludes vanishing from the nonvanishing of a local class, not of c_K itself: it is the rank-zero companion of (a).

nodes.title: Simultaneous localisation of eigenclasses in Howard's self-dual setting
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, R principal artinian of length k with residue characteristic p, and (T, F, 𝓛) a Selmer triple such that (T, F) and (T*, F*) satisfy H.0–H.5 of ES.5/howard-hypotheses, with 𝓛 ⊆ 𝓛_k(T). (a) Let s ≥ 1 and c₁, …, c_n ∈ H¹(K, T̄) nonzero residual classes, where T̄ = T/mT, with c_i in the ε_i-eigenspace of complex conjugation τ. If p > n, a positive proportion of primes ℓ ∈ 𝓛_s(T) satisfy loc_ℓ(c_i) ≠ 0 for every i. (b) Let p > 3, H(n) = H¹_{F(n)}(K, T), ρ(n)^± = dim_{R/m} H(n)[m]^± and r(n) = max(ρ(n)⁺, ρ(n)⁻). If n ∈ N(𝓛) has r(n) > 1 and 0 ≠ c ∈ H(n), and 𝓛 contains 𝓛_t(T) for some t ≥ max(k, s), a positive proportion of ℓ ∈ 𝓛_t(T) outside the prime factors of n satisfy loc_ℓ(c) ≠ 0 and r(nℓ) < r(n).
hypotheses: H.0–H.5 for (T, F) and (T*, F*); 𝓛 ⊆ 𝓛_k(T)
In (a) all classes have coefficients T̄. In (b) deep primes must belong to 𝓛, not merely to the ambient set 𝓛_s(T).
proofSteps: (a): with F the field of H.2 and L the Galois closure of K(T/m^s, μ_{p^s}) over ℚ, restriction H¹(K, T̄) → Hom(G_L, T̄)^{Gal(L/K)} is injective by H.2. Each c_i cuts out E_i/L with an F_p-vector space G_i = Gal(E_i/L) split into τ-eigenspaces; c_i is nonzero on G_i^+ because otherwise R·c_i(G_i) would be a proper G_K-submodule contradicting H.1 and H.5(a).

The bad sets H_i = {η ∈ G_L^+ : c_i(η) = 0} have Haar measure at most 1/p, so for p > n their union is not everything; write a good η as (τσ)² and use Chebotarev for Frobenius τσ in Gal(E₁⋯E_n/ℚ); such ℓ lie in 𝓛_s(T) as in Mazur–Rubin, Lemma 3.5.6(i). This is Howard's Lemma 1.6.2 argument with n classes.

(b): if both ρ(n)^± ≥ 1 identify residual modified Selmer groups with H(n)[m] by cartesianness and Howard Lemma 1.3.3, then apply (a) to nonzero residual eigenclasses from both signs and a nonzero socle multiple of c (three classes, so p > 3), and use Howard's parity Lemma 1.5.3 to get ρ(nℓ)^± = ρ(n)^± − 1; if ρ(n)^∓ = 0 apply (a) to two residual classes. Choose primes in 𝓛_t ⊆ 𝓛 outside n, so nℓ remains an allowed conductor.
acceptance: For n = 1 and p > 1, (a) is the single-class Chebotarev selection in each eigenspace.
For n = 4, (a) requires p > 4, which is why the connectivity of core vertices in ES.5/self-dual-core-vertex-rigidity assumes p > 4.
Iterating (b) from any n reaches a core vertex (r = 1) in at most r(n) − 1 steps.

nodes.title: Divisibility profile and primitivity of self-dual Kolyvagin systems
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with p > 4 and (T, F, 𝓛) a Selmer triple over an imaginary quadratic K with (T, F) and (T*, F*) satisfying H.0–H.5 (ES.5/howard-hypotheses) and 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T) for some s ≥ 1. For κ ∈ KS(T, F, 𝓛) and k ≥ 1 let κ^{(k)} be its reduction in KS(T^{(k)}, F, 𝓛^{(k)}), H^{(k)}(n) = H¹_{F(n)}(K, T^{(k)}), and ρ(n) the residual Selmer rank of ES.5/self-dual-eigenspace-localisation. Define: (i) for n ∈ N, M(n) = ind(κ_n) = max{j : κ_n ∈ m^j H¹(K, T/I_nT)} (∞ if κ_n = 0), in the residual-surjective anticyclotomic elliptic setting, M_r = min{M(n) : ν(n) = r} and M_∞(κ) = lim_{r→∞} M_r, which exists because M_r ≥ M_{r+1}; (ii) use the truncated index ind_k(x) = max{0 ≤ a ≤ k : x ∈ m^a H^{(k)}(n)}, so ind_k(0) = k, and set δ_k = min_{n∈N^{(k)}} ind_k(κ_n^{(k)}), ∂^{(∞)}(κ) = sup_k δ_k; (iii) d_k = ind_k(κ_n^{(k)}) at any core vertex n ∈ N^{(k)} and d(κ) = lim_k d_k. The indices satisfy d_k = min(d(κ), k), so their stable value, rather than each finite-level index, is independent of k. κ is primitive if ∂^{(∞)}(κ) = 0, equivalently if its reduction in KS(T/mT, F, 𝓛) is nonzero. Properties: d(κ) ≥ ∂^{(∞)}(κ); d(κ) = 0 if and only if κ is primitive; d(κ) = ∞ if and only if κ = 0; assuming odd rank in the general self-dual setting, κ_n^{(k)}R^{(k)} = m^{d(κ)+length(M^{(k)}(n))}H^{(k)}(n) for n ∈ N^{(2k−1)}. In the anticyclotomic elliptic setting with residual surjectivity, d(κ) = M_∞(κ) whenever κ₁ ≠ 0. Moreover, in the anticyclotomic elliptic setting of ES.1/twist-error-constants with residual surjectivity and p ≥ 3, the stable index can be computed on any 𝓛_e = {ℓ : a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p^e} ⊆ 𝓛 with e ≫ 0: M_{∞,N(𝓛_e)}(κ) = M_{∞,N(𝓛)}(κ). This extends ES.5/divisibility-invariants from Mazur–Rubin's systems over ℚ to Howard's self-dual systems over K.
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring, p > 4; H.0–H.5 for (T, F) and (T*, F*); 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T)
for the computation on 𝓛_e: the elliptic anticyclotomic setting with residual surjectivity and p ≥ 3

For the stub formula and d_k core construction: odd rank ε = 1, as in Zanarella Lemma 2.3.1. Nonzero κ₁ implies this in the structure theorem. M_r and M_∞ monotonicity are asserted only in the BCGS elliptic setting.
proofSteps: Compatibility of truncated core indices: by ES.5/self-dual-core-vertex-rigidity there are d_k with κ_n^{(k)}R^{(k)} ≅ m^{d_k}R^{(k)} at every core vertex n ∈ N^{(k)}; d_k ≤ d_{k+1}, with equality when d_k < k; d(κ) = lim d_k.

The formula on N^{(2k−1)} is proved by induction on k + max(ρ(n)⁺, ρ(n)⁻) using ES.5/self-dual-eigenspace-localisation(b), the Kolyvagin relation, ES.5/howard-stub and the stub refinement loc_ℓ(m^d S(n)) = 0 ⇔ loc_ℓ(m^d S(nℓ)) = 0.

d(κ) = 0 ⇔ primitive: if κ^{(1)} ≠ 0 some κ_n^{(1)} ≠ 0 and the formula with k = 1 forces d = 0. d(κ) = ∞ ⇔ κ = 0 by the vanishing criterion of ES.5/self-dual-core-vertex-rigidity. The identification with M_∞ uses the core-vertex computation of the refined structure theorem (BCGS, proof of Theorem 2.2.2).

Computation on 𝓛_e: if the minimum M_r is attained at n with a prime ℓ₀ | n outside 𝓛_e, take the residual eigencomponent κ̄^s of κ_n^{(δ+1)} and a nonzero class c of the opposite eigenspace with no condition at ℓ₀ (global duality, as in ES.1/residual-two-class-detection(b)); ES.1/error-tolerant-chebotarev(c), with zero loss under residual surjectivity, gives ℓ ∈ 𝓛_e with loc_ℓ κ̄^s ≠ 0 and loc_ℓ c ≠ 0. The Kolyvagin relations and the sum of local pairings of c with κ̄_ℓ over ℓ and ℓ₀ show M(nℓ/ℓ₀) = M(n); repeat.

nodes.title: Rigidity of self-dual Kolyvagin systems at core vertices
nodes.statement: Let R be principal artinian of length k with p > 4, (T, F, 𝓛) as in ES.5/self-dual-eigenspace-localisation with ε = 1 in the Cassels decomposition of ES.5/cassels-structure (odd rank), and 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T) for some s ≥ 1. A core vertex is n ∈ N with ρ(n) = 1, equivalently H¹_{F(n)}(K, T) ≅ R. (a) For a core vertex n and nℓ ∈ N the following are equivalent: nℓ is a core vertex; loc_ℓ is injective on H(n); loc_ℓ is injective on H(nℓ); loc_ℓ H̄(n) ≠ 0; loc_ℓ H̄(nℓ) ≠ 0, where H̄ denotes the modified Selmer group with coefficients T̄, identified with H(−)[m]; and then (loc^s_ℓ)^{-1} ∘ φ^fs_ℓ ∘ loc_ℓ : H(n) → H(nℓ) is an isomorphism. (b) The graph of core vertices, with edges n — nℓ, is connected. (c) For every κ ∈ KS(T, F, 𝓛) there is 0 ≤ d ≤ k with κ_nR = m^d H(n) at every core vertex n, and d = k iff κ = 0.
hypotheses: R principal artinian, p > 4, H.0–H.5 for (T, F) and (T*, F*), odd rank, 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T)
proofSteps: For (a), cartesianness and Howard Lemma 1.3.3 identify the residual strict Selmer group with the socle of the full strict group. A finite module over a local artinian ring is zero iff its socle is zero. Thus nonzero localization of the one-dimensional residual H̄(n) is equivalent to injectivity on the cyclic full H(n); nonzero localization of H(n) alone is insufficient. The parity formula then characterizes nℓ as a core vertex. At both core vertices the injective finite and singular localizations between free rank-one modules are isomorphisms, yielding the full-module isomorphism through φ^fs_ℓ and the Kolyvagin relation.

(b): induct on ν(lcm(n, m)) − ν(gcd(n, m)); if nℓ is not a core vertex, ES.5/self-dual-eigenspace-localisation(a) with four classes (p > 4) gives r with nrℓ, nr and mr core vertices, joining n to m by paths.
(c): (a) and (b) give the common d; if d = k then every κ_n vanishes, by induction on r(n) using ES.5/self-dual-eigenspace-localisation(b) and the Kolyvagin relation.
acceptance: For R = R/m (k = 1), (c) says κ_n ≠ 0 at one core vertex iff at all core vertices.
(c) is the self-dual analogue of Mazur–Rubin's rigidity at core vertices (ES.4/core-vertices, ES.5/rank-one-module-theorem); it does not assume core rank one over ℚ.
Without p > 4 the connectivity argument in (b) has no prime satisfying the four localisation conditions; the theorem is not claimed for p = 3.
Over R = ℤ/p², multiplication by p on R is nonzero but not injective and vanishes on the socle pR. This distinguishes full-group nonvanishing from the residual nonvanishing criterion in (a).

nodes.title: Exact length of the Tate–Shafarevich module from a self-dual Kolyvagin system
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field Φ, D = Φ/R, (T, F, 𝓛) a Selmer triple over an imaginary quadratic K with (T, F) and (T*, F*) satisfying H.0–H.5, p > 4 and 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T) for some s ≥ 1. If κ ∈ KS(T, F, 𝓛) has κ₁ ≠ 0, then H¹_F(K, T) is free of rank one, H¹_F(K, A) ≅ D ⊕ M ⊕ M for a finite R-module M, and length_R(M) = length_R(H¹_F(K, T)/R·κ₁) − d(κ), with d(κ) of ES.5/self-dual-divisibility-profile. In particular length_R(M) ≤ length_R(H¹_F(K, T)/R·κ₁), with equality iff κ is primitive. In the elliptic setting of Burungale–Castella–Grossi–Skinner (anticyclotomic twists T_pE ⊗ R(α) with α ≡ 1 mod m^m, p > 3 and residual surjectivity), where d(κ) = M_∞(κ), this reads length_R Ш(W_{α^{-1}}/K) = 2(M₀(κ) − M_∞(κ)) with M₀(κ) = ind(κ₁) and M_∞(κ) the stable index.
hypotheses: R a DVR, p > 4 (p > 3 in the elliptic setting with residual surjectivity), H.0–H.5 for (T, F) and (T*, F*), 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s(T)
κ₁ ≠ 0
proofSteps: Freeness of H¹_F(K, T) and the decomposition H¹_F(K, A) ≅ D ⊕ M ⊕ M are ES.5/howard-dvr-theorem.

For k large H^{(k)}(1) ≅ R/m^k ⊕ M ⊕ M with λ = length(M) = λ^{(k)}(1); the formula of ES.5/self-dual-divisibility-profile at n = 1 gives κ₁^{(k)}R^{(k)} = m^{d(κ)+λ}H^{(k)}(1), and for k > d(κ) + λ the injectivity of H(1)/m^k → H^{(k)}(1) gives κ₁R = m^{λ+d(κ)}H(1), i.e. λ = ind(κ₁) − d(κ).

The equality case follows from d(κ) = 0 iff κ is primitive. In BCGS's form, the induction of Castella–Grossi–Skinner's Theorem 6.1.1 with zero error (residual surjectivity) reaches a core vertex n_ρ with ind(κ_{n_ρ}) = M_∞(κ), and Lemma 2.2.4 gives ind(κ₁) = M_∞ + length(M), so length(M ⊕ M) = 2(M₀ − M_∞).
acceptance: Primitive κ: length(M) equals the index of κ₁, so the Kolyvagin bound of ES.5/howard-dvr-theorem is sharp.
κ′ = π^aκ for primitive κ: index of κ′₁ grows by a and d grows by a, so length(M) is unchanged, as it must be.

For E/ℚ of analytic rank one over K and the Heegner system, combined with Gross–Zagier this gives the exact p-part of #Ш(E/K) up to the defect 2M_∞, which vanishes exactly when the system is primitive.

nodes.title: Equality in Howard's Λ-adic bound for Λ-primitive self-dual systems
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ have conductor N prime to D_K, p ∤ ND_K, p ≥ 5, good reduction at p and surjective residual representation, K∞/K the anticyclotomic ℤ_p-extension, Λ = ℤ_p[[Gal(K∞/K)]], 𝐓 = T_pE ⊗ Λ with the Selmer structure F_Λ of ES.8/self-dual-lambda-adic-kolyvagin-bound (ordinary or, in the supersingular case, the Castella–Wan structure), and X = Hom(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐀), ℚ_p/ℤ_p). A Λ-adic Kolyvagin system κ ∈ KS(𝐓, F_Λ, 𝓛) with 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s is Λ-primitive if for every height-one prime 𝔓 there is k with nonzero image in KS(𝐓/(𝔓, m^k), F_Λ, 𝓛_j) for all j ≥ s, and primitive if its image in KS(𝐓/m, F_Λ, 𝓛) is nonzero; primitive implies Λ-primitive. If κ₁ ≠ 0 then (a) H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓) is torsion-free of Λ-rank one; (b) X ∼ Λ ⊕ M ⊕ M for a torsion Λ-module M with char(M) = char(M)^ι; (c) char(M) divides char(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓)/Λκ₁), with equality if κ is Λ-primitive.
hypotheses: E/ℚ, (N, D_K) = 1, p ∤ ND_K, p ≥ 5, good reduction at p, residual surjectivity
κ ∈ KS(𝐓, F_Λ, 𝓛) with 𝓛 ⊇ 𝓛_s and κ₁ ≠ 0
proofSteps: (a), (b) and the divisibility in (c) are ES.8/self-dual-lambda-adic-kolyvagin-bound.

For 𝔓 = (g) ≠ (p), use 𝔔_m = (g + p^m). For m sufficiently large, Hensel approximation identifies the finite ℤ_p-orders Λ/𝔓 and Λ/𝔔_m as rings, and the normalization index is bounded. Specialization control and the DVR exact structure theorem give m·d·ord_𝔓 char(M) = m·d·ord_𝔓 char(H¹/Λκ₁) − f_m d(κ^{(𝔔_m)}) + O(1), where d = rank_{ℤ_p}(Λ/𝔓) and f_m is the residue degree of S_{𝔔_m}; f_m is bounded. This branch does not cover 𝔓 = (p).

For 𝔓 ≠ (p), Λ-primitivity supplies a nonzero finite quotient system and a core vertex at a fixed level k. The corresponding quotient representations and cartesian Selmer conditions agree along sufficiently close 𝔔_m, bounding d(κ^{(𝔔_m)}) by k. For 𝔓 = (p), take 𝔔_m = (p + T^m); this polynomial is Eisenstein, Λ/𝔔_m is already its normalization with uniformizer T and residue degree 1, and length_{ℤ_p} Λ/(p^a, p+T^m) = ma. The torsion-module length slope is therefore m·ord_(p), with the other characteristic factors contributing O(1). The control bound depends on the normalization index, which is 1 here. For m ≥ k, Λ/(p+T^m, (p,T)^k) = Λ/(p, (p,T)^k), so Λ-primitivity and finite-level core-vertex rigidity again bound the specialized defect. This finite-quotient argument avoids treating Λ/(p) as a finite ℤ_p-order. The erroneous combined branch in the source is recorded as E903.
Primitive implies Λ-primitive: a residually nonzero system has d = 0, so its image at every height-one prime 𝔓 (with (𝔓, m) = m) is nonzero with k(𝔓) = 1.
acceptance: For the Heegner Kolyvagin system, primitivity (Kolyvagin's conjecture in its refined form) gives the anticyclotomic main conjecture equality char(M) = char(H¹/Λκ₁^{Hg}).
A system that is Λ-primitive but has vanishing residual image is allowed: (c) still gives equality.
Scaling κ by a non-unit of Λ destroys Λ-primitivity at the primes dividing it and strictly enlarges the right-hand side of (c).

nodes.title: Λ-adic divisibility including the augmentation prime
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ, p ∤ 2N good ordinary, K imaginary quadratic with (D_K, Np) = 1, every prime dividing N split in K, p split in K, and E(K)[p] = 0, Λ the anticyclotomic Iwasawa algebra with augmentation ideal (γ − 1), 𝐓 = T_pE ⊗ Λ with the ordinary Selmer structure F_Λ, X = H¹_{F_Λ}(K, M_E)^∨ and S = H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓). If κ ∈ KS(𝐓, F_Λ, 𝓛_E) has κ₁ ≠ 0, then S has Λ-rank one and there is a finitely generated torsion Λ-module M with X ∼ Λ ⊕ M ⊕ M and char_Λ(M) dividing char_Λ(S/Λκ₁) in Λ[1/p]: unlike ES.8/error-tolerant-self-dual-lambda-adic-bound, the prime (γ − 1) is not inverted. For the higher-weight setting listed below, Keller–Yin Theorem3.0.5 asserts the integral divisibility in Λ. This plan establishes its away-from-(π) argument; the integral branch is a conditional target until a uniform-error argument at (π), or a compatible µ(M)=0 comparison, is supplied.
hypotheses: E/ℚ, p ∤ 2N good ordinary, (D_K, Np) = 1, E(K)[p] = 0; every prime dividing N and p split in K
κ ∈ KS(𝐓, F_Λ, 𝓛_E) with κ₁ ≠ 0

For the higher-weight branch: f is a normalized weight-2r newform of trivial nebentype, p∤2N is ordinary and Eisenstein, O is the coefficient completion, T is its chosen self-dual-twist lattice with H⁰(K,T/πT)=0, every prime dividing N splits in K, p splits in K, and D_K is odd, prime to Np and not −3 (Keller–Yin introduction and §3).
proofSteps: At height-one primes 𝔓 ≠ (p), (γ − 1) the argument of ES.8/error-tolerant-self-dual-lambda-adic-bound applies: specialise at 𝔔_m = (g + p^m) and use ES.4/howard-descent-with-errors with error E_α bounded in m.

At 𝔓 = (γ − 1) the specialisations are characters α_m ≡ 1 mod p^m, where E_α grows with m; replace that input by ES.4/uniform-near-trivial-bound(a), whose error is independent of m, so ord_{(γ−1)} char(M) ≤ ord_{(γ−1)} char(S/Λκ₁).

For higher weight, the same argument proves the divisibility in Λ[1/π]. For the integral claim, perturb (π) by (π+T^m). The coefficient order has O-rank m, so an error known only to depend on rank_O(R) can grow with m and cannot be discarded after division by m. Howard’s clean finite-level bound has zero error, whereas Keller–Yin §3 only states errors depending on that rank. The plan must provide a uniform (or o(m)) error along these quotients, or a proved µ(M)=0 result together with its ordinary Selmer dictionary. The cited sentence in Theorem3.0.5 is not that missing argument; this review leaves the integral branch unresolved, without declaring its conclusion false.
acceptance: If moreover H¹_F(K, E[p^∞]) has ℤ_p-corank one, the error-tolerant theorem already gave the divisibility at (γ − 1); this theorem removes that corank hypothesis.
For the Heegner Kolyvagin system this gives one divisibility of the Heegner point main conjecture in Λ[1/p] at Eisenstein primes.

nodes.title: Derivative classes and the key relation under the alternative rigidity conditions
nodes.statement: Let c be an Euler system for (T, 𝒦, N) satisfying Rubin's condition (ii)′(b) or (ii)′(c) of ES.2/rigidity-variants in place of the existence of a ℤ_p^d-extension in 𝒦, and assume T^{G_{K(1)}} = 0. (ii)′(b): c_{K(r)} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K(r), T) for every r, and some γ ∈ G_K is trivial on K(1)(μ_{p^∞}, (O_K^×)^{1/p^∞}) with γ − 1 injective on T. (ii)′(c): c_{K(r)} ∈ S^{Σ_p}(K(r), T) for every r, Fr_q^n − 1 is injective on T for every q ∤ N and every power n of p, and the classes c_{K(r)} satisfy the congruence of ES.3/congruence. Then there is a power m of p, independent of M, such that for r ∈ R_{K,Mm} the derivative classes κ_{K,r,M} are defined and satisfy (a) κ_{K,r,M} is finite at every place not dividing pr, and (b) the singular part of κ_{K,rq,M} at q is φ^fs_q of the finite part of κ_{K,r,M} at q. Under (ii)′(b), (b) rests on the identity P(γ | T; 1)·(N_q γ d̂(x_{F(rq)}) − P(Fr_q^{-1} | T*; Fr_q^{-1}) γ d̂(x_{F(r)})) = 0 in W_{M′} for a power M′ of p divisible by M·P(γ | T; 1), proved with auxiliary primes l in place of the ℤ_p-tower. Consequently Rubin's Theorems II.2.2, II.2.3 and II.2.10 (ES.4/rubin-bound) hold with the same conclusions.
hypotheses: c satisfies the corestriction relations of an Euler system and (ii)′(b) or (ii)′(c); T^{G_{K(1)}} = 0
r ∈ R_{K,Mm}, with m depending on T and c but not on M
proofSteps: Construction: T^{G_{K(1)}} = 0 gives T^{G_{K(r)}} = 0 for every r (Rubin, Lemma IV.2.5(i)), so with 𝕋 = Maps(G_K, T) the sequence 0 → 𝕋^{G_{F(r)}} → (𝕋/T)^{G_{F(r)}} → H¹(F(r), T) → 0 is exact and replaces the inverse limit of Proposition IV.4.7; lift c through it as in ES.3/lifting-to-induced-module(b), project to (𝕎_M/W_M)^{G_{F(r)}} and define κ_{F,r,M} as in ES.3/derivative-class.

(a): ES.3/derivative-classes-unramified(d) needs only that the Euler-system classes are unramified away from p, which (ii)′(b) and (ii)′(c) include as an assumption (under (ii)′(a) it came from the tower).

(b) under (ii)′(b): with n = |μ_{p^∞} ∩ K| choose, by Chebotarev, a prime l with Fr_l = γ on K(1)(μ_{nM′}, (O_K^×)^{1/(nM′)}, W_{M′}), Fr_l = 1 on K(rq), and Fr_l ≠ 1 on K(λ^{1/(np)}) where λO_K = q^h, h the order of q in the class group. Then nM′ | [K(l) : K] and the decomposition group of q in Gal(K(l)/K) has order at least M′. The Euler relation makes P(Fr_l^{-1} | T*; Fr_l^{-1})c_{K(r)} a norm from K(rl), and P(Fr_l^{-1} | T*; Fr_l^{-1}) ≡ P(γ | T; 1) mod M in O[Gal(K(rq)/K)]; the proof of ES.3/key-relation(c) then runs with K(l)/K in place of the tower.
(b) under (ii)′(c): reverse the argument of ES.3/congruence, deducing the key relation of ES.3/key-relation(c) from the congruence and the injectivity of Fr_q^n − 1.
The bounds of ES.4/rubin-bound use only κ_{K,r,M} for r ∈ R_{K,Mm} with these properties; the extra factor m does not affect them.
acceptance: Cyclotomic units without a ℤ_p-tower: for χ a nontrivial even character of conductor prime to p, the twisted family of (ζ_m − 1)(ζ_m^{-1} − 1) satisfies (ii)′(b) and (ii)′(c) but not (ii)′(a), and the theorem gives |A_L^χ| = [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}] (Rubin, Example IX.1.1 and Theorem IX.1.2; the arithmetic belongs to EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture).
Without any rigidity condition the statement fails: the family with c_F = 0 for F ≠ K and c_K arbitrary is an Euler system (ES.2/rigidity-variants(a)).
Under (ii)′(a) the theorem reduces to ES.3/derivative-local-properties with m = 1.

nodes.title: Uniform cokernel bound for a separated pairing over orders
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space, B⊆End_{ℚ_p}(V) a semisimple ℚ_p-algebra, Λ_B a ℤ_p-order in B, and T⊆V a full Λ_B-stable lattice. Put D=End_B(V)^op and R={d∈D:T d⊆T}. For N≥1 let X be a finite left Λ_B/p^NΛ_B-module and W a finite right R/p^NR-module. A ℤ_p-bilinear pairing X×W→T/p^NT is Λ_B-linear on X and R-linear on W and induces injective maps i:W→Hom_{Λ_B}(X,T/p^NT) and j:X→Hom_R(W,T/p^NT). Choose a maximal order R_max⊇R and put Λ_max={b∈B:b(T R_max)⊆T R_max}. For central non-zero-divisors c,d in R_max with cΛ_max⊆Λ_B and dR_max⊆R, one has cd·Coker(j)=0, using the common-center action. Such conductor elements exist and are independent of N. In particular, when both orders are maximal, j is surjective.
hypotheses: Finite X and W are essential; the infinite direct-sum pairing violates the printed unrestricted formulation (E907).
Characteristic zero and semisimplicity; retain both separatedness maps.
The center identifications and maximal-order/Morita facts are the precise CA.7 Part II supplier contract.
proofSteps: Enlarge T to T R_max and extend the two separated pairing images to modules over the maximal orders. Multiplication by c kills the cokernel after this enlargement, and d kills the kernel of the comparison back to T/p^NT, so the final cokernel is annihilated by cd.

At maximal orders use the semisimple centralizer decomposition and Morita equivalence to reduce, including multiplicities of simple factors, to a matrix order over the maximal order of a local division algebra. Finite W is a finite sum of cyclic right modules there.

Lift the pairing image to a sublattice of a finite power of T. Separatedness supplies a nonzero image modulo the division uniformizer. The simple residual matrix module and Nakayama give the one-factor case. Heredity/projectivity splits projection to the final factor; induction gives the full lattice and hence surjectivity. These are the arguments of Nekovář Proposition6.4.3, pp.39–40, with the finite-module hypothesis made explicit.
acceptance: For B=ℚ_p, T=ℤ_p, R=Λ_B=ℤ_p and a perfect finite pairing modulo p^N, c=d=1 and j is an isomorphism.
For X=W=⊕_{i∈ℕ}𝔽_p with the coordinate pairing, i and j are injective but j lands in the direct sum inside Hom(W,𝔽_p)=∏𝔽_p and is not surjective. The target excludes this infinite example.
A conductor power that works for the two fixed lattice orders works for every N; increasing N must not increase the proposed annihilator.

Multivariable Iwasawa algebras Λ = O[[Γ]] ≅ O⟦T_1, …, T_d⟧ for Γ ≅ Z_p^d: noetherian, regular local of dimension d + 1, hence factorial; pseudo-null modules (annihilated by an ideal of height ≥ 2, not finite when d ≥ 2), pseudo-isomorphisms and characteristic ideals over them, with multiplicativity in exact sequences and pseudo-isomorphism invariance. Rubin's Theorems II.3.2–II.3.4 and II.3.8 are stated for every d ≥ 1 (the stage's own remaining item 'Multivariable algebras O⟦T₁, …, T_d⟧').

Twisting of characteristic ideals and annihilators: for a character ρ: Γ → O^×, Tw_ρ: Λ → Λ the O-algebra automorphism γ ↦ ρ(γ)γ, and a finitely generated torsion Λ-module B, Tw_ρ(char(B ⊗ ρ)) = char(B) and Tw_ρ(Ann_Λ(B ⊗ ρ)) = Ann_Λ(B) (Rubin, Euler systems, Lemma VI.1.2); Tw_ρ preserves heights of ideals.

For Λ=O⟦T⟧, P=(g)≠(π) distinguished, Q_m=(g+p^m): for a finite torsion Λ-module Z, length_{ℤ_p}(Z/Q_mZ)=m·rank_{ℤ_p}(Λ/P)·ord_P char(Z)+O(1); for m large Λ/Q_m is a finite ℤ_p-order isomorphic to Λ/P. For P=(π), instead use the Eisenstein Q_m=(T^m+π), already normal with uniformizer T; length_{ℤ_p}Λ/(π^a,T^m+π)=a m f_O, where f_O=[O/π:𝔽_p]. The normalization index here is1. This branch does not identify Λ/(π) with a finite ℤ_p-order; (T^m+p) is not a valid uniformizer perturbation over a ramified O. Topological Nakayama's lemma over Λ = O[[Γ]]: a compact Λ-module X with X/𝔐X (or X/JX, J the augmentation ideal) finitely generated over O is finitely generated over Λ. Used for the finite generation of X∞ (Rubin, Lemma VII.4.1).

The O-algebra automorphisms Tw_ρ of Λ = O[[Γ]] induced by γ ↦ ρ(γ)γ for continuous characters ρ: Γ → O^×, with Tw_ρ ∘ Tw_ρ' = Tw_{ρρ'}, and the involution ι (γ ↦ γ^{-1}); compatibility with the projections Λ → O[Gal(F/K)].

For a Z_p-extension K∞/K, 𝐓 = T ⊗ Λ and Σ finite containing p, ∞ and the ramified primes: H^i(K_Σ/K, 𝐓) and H^i(K_v, 𝐓) (v | p) are finitely generated Λ-modules, H²(K_v, 𝐓) is Λ-torsion, and H¹(K_Σ/K, 𝐓) is Λ-torsion-free when T̄^{G_K} = 0 (Mazur–Rubin, Lemmas 5.3.4–5.3.5, after Greenberg and Perrin-Riou); and H²(K_v, 𝐓)/𝔓 ≅ H²(K_v, 𝐓/𝔓𝐓) (cohomological dimension two).

Global class field theory in the form: the inertia subgroup at a finite prime v of the Galois group of an abelian pro-p extension of a number field is the image of the pro-p completion of O_v^×; hence Z_p^d-extensions are unramified outside p; and the maximal abelian p-extension unramified everywhere and split at the primes above p of a field corresponds to the p-part of its class group modulo those primes.

For finite free ℤ_p X with continuous Ẑ-action, supply cochains-inverse-limit, milnor-sequence, mittag-leffler-lim-one and continuous-section-long-exact. H¹ of each X/p^aX is finite (determined by topological Frobenius), so lim¹ H¹=0; discrete cd_p=1 then gives compact H²=0 and H¹(X)→H¹(X/MX) surjective. Restrict to this finite-free setting unless stronger limit hypotheses are proved.
